label: Joslyn (1995), Semantic Control Systems, §3.3, Definition 28 (Control₂)
source_location: §3.3 Control Theory, Definition 28, p. 103 (from the 2026-08-27 page-image transcription section)
verbatim: Definition 28 (Control₂) A control₁ system CS = ⟨C, O⟩ is also a control₂ system if the variation in the constraint₁ on O, induced by C's variation, is itself constrained₂.
display_form: A control₁ system CS = ⟨C, O⟩ is also a control₂ system if the variation in the constraint₁ on O, induced by C's variation, is itself constrained₂.

primitives.scope_note: Joslyn's word for the metasystem CS = ⟨C, O⟩ of Definition 25, in which the actions of the controller C result in a constraint₂ on the freedom of the object of control O; it is the antecedent kind on which control₂ is predicated.
Joslyn's word for the kind of system defined here: a control₁ system whose second-order variation in the constraint₁ on O, induced by C's variation, is itself constrained₂.
The author's word, carried into this definition, for the systemic constraint C := X − S of Definition 6; here it is what C places on O and what may itself vary.
The author's word, the participial form of constraint₂ (Definition 15, the reduction of some variety), predicated here of the second-order variation in the constraint₁ on O.

The author's word for the varying of a component or of a constraint over its state space; used here at two levels (C's variation, and the variation in the constraint₁ on O) without further formal analysis in the definition itself.

admits.label: Thermodynamic system O in a systematically varying thermal environment C
admits.gloss: Joslyn's worked example: once O's envelope of variation stays constant while C's temperature changes systematically, the pair CS = ⟨C, O⟩ is declared a control₂ system.
admits.verbatim: That is, as Cs temperature changed, O's envelope of variation remained constant. Under these conditions, CS is now a control2 system.

admits.label: Thermostat (human-engineered machine)
admits.gloss: Joslyn offers engineered machines such as thermostats as familiar instances of control₂ systems.
admits.verbatim: We are quite familiar with control2 systems which are artifacts, for example human-engineered machines like thermostats.

refuses.label: System governed only by a stable equilibrium (the damped spring of Eq. 26)
refuses.gloss: Joslyn rules that mere passive stability is not control₂, since varying the free parameters varies the constraint₁ on O and hence the equilibrium point.
refuses.verbatim: It is clear that a system governed only by a stable equilibrium, as in (26), is not a controlg system: a variation of the free parameters causes a corresponding variation of the constraintj on O, and thus of x*.

refuses.label: Boiling liquid
refuses.gloss: A dynamic equilibrium whose rate tracks the heat input; Joslyn states explicitly that it is not controlled₂.
refuses.verbatim: The boiling activity is in dynamic equilibrium, but it is not controlled2.

refuses.label: Spinning top
refuses.gloss: The spin stabilises the axis of revolution, but a tilt of the table moves it; Joslyn notes that a controlled₂ position would resist the perturbation.
refuses.verbatim: The torque generated by its active spinning creates a stable position of the axis of revolution, but a tilt to the table top will cause that center to move. If the position were controlled2, then it would resist that environmental perturbation.
